correctness.rationale: The theorem normalizes by each finite vertex-set Euclidean diameter, permits empty parts and asserts every integer k>=1. For each distance-square threshold t, the far-distance graph G_t with edges iff squared distance>t has chi(G_t)<=k exactly when a k-part partition has all squared diameters <=t. Independent code regenerated all five coordinate-derived distance spectra and computed the chromatic profiles tetra [4,1], cube [8,4,2,1], octa [6,2,1], icosa [12,4,2,1], dodeca [20,10,5,4,2,1], including a complete DSATUR decision search on each finite graph. Inspected source exact Q(phi) verifier validates 19 witness color vectors and lower bounds: no large admissible classes at tight thresholds, the 12 possible dodecahedral size-five classes cannot cover 20 with four colors at t=4, and none of the 820 disjoint pairs of 100 admissible seven-sets at t=8 leaves admissible six-set. All pair-distance levels are included; hence no untested intermediate cutoffs. These are exhaustive fixed finite certificates, not a general arbitrary finite-set theorem.
